newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks raise prime rate after Fed action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks raise prime rate after Fed action.

text.p: Major banks including Citibank increased their key lending rates on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve moved to push an important short-term interest rate higher.

Banc One, the nation's 10th-largest bank, was the first to boost its prime rate to 8.50 percent from 8.25 percent after the Fed said it would allow the federal funds rate to rise one-quarter of a percentage point to 5.50 percent.

The prime rate is traditionally the lowest rate that banks charge their most creditworthy corporate clients. But it has become a benchmark for many types of consumer loans, including credit cards, adjustable mortgages and home equity loans.
Citibank, a unit of Citicorp, and Central Fidelity Banks Inc. of Richmond, Va., also raised their rates to the same level.
The Banc One and Central Fidelity prime rate changes were effective as of Wednesday, but Citibank said its change was effective as of Tuesday.

A statement released by the Fed said the slight tightening in monetary conditions was viewed as a "prudent step that affords greater assurance of prolonging the current economic expansion by sustaining the existing low inflation environment through the rest of this year and next."
The federal funds rate is the interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans.
Tuesday's prime rate hikes were the first in more than two years. The central bank last tightened monetary policy on Feb. 1, 1995.
